column1: Gap Summary — Normative Coverage by Requirement

column5: RFC gaps (2 of 9): Ephemeral agent or sub-agent identity; Distinguish upstream from downstream delegation participants. Partial RFC coverage (4): Represent chains of delegation actors; Runtime retrieval of participant identity metadata; Persistent or key-bound client/subject identity; Local vs. global scoping of participant identifiers. Normative RFC coverage (3 sub-requirements): RFC 6749, RFC 8693, RFC 9068.

RFC gaps (1 of 4): Preserve accountability across multiple delegation hops. Partial RFC coverage (1): Prevent identity collapse in multi-hop delegation chains. Normative RFC coverage (2 sub-requirements): RFC 8693, RFC 9068.

RFC gaps (3 of 7): Tool-invocation-level authorization constraints; Workflow or transaction-scoped delegation constraints; Guarantee of authority monotonicity. Partial RFC coverage (1): Narrowing of delegated authority during token exchange. Normative RFC coverage (3 sub-requirements): RFC 6749, RFC 8707, RFC 9068, RFC 9396.

RFC gaps (2 of 6): Designate a named enforcement actor for each delegation constraint type; Define enforcement responsibilities across heterogeneous agent platforms. Partial RFC coverage (1): Reject execution when authorization_details type is unknown. Normative RFC coverage (3 sub-requirements): RFC 6749, RFC 6750, RFC 7662, RFC 9396.

RFC gaps (4 of 10): Delegator role; Delegate agent role; Downstream delegation participant role; Delegation ancestry semantics. Normative RFC coverage (6 sub-requirements): RFC 6749, RFC 8414, RFC 8693, RFC 9068, RFC 9635, RFC 9728.

RFC gaps (3 of 7): Downstream delegation lifetime bounded by upstream; Normative relationship between upstream and downstream lifetime constraints; Renewal and reauthorization semantics for persistent delegation chains. Partial RFC coverage (1): Revocation as effective shortening of token lifetime. Normative RFC coverage (3 sub-requirements): RFC 6750, RFC 7662, RFC 9068.

RFC gaps (4 of 9): Cascading revocation to downstream delegation artifacts; Subtree revocation; Partial delegation revocation; Revocation behavior during in-progress delegated execution. Partial RFC coverage (2): Revocation latency and consistency; Freshness / availability declaration. Normative RFC coverage (3 sub-requirements): RFC 6750, RFC 7009, RFC 7662.

RFC gaps (3 of 8): Delegation ancestry validation across multi-hop chains; Delegation-depth validation; Delegation provenance validation. Partial RFC coverage (1): Actor and authorized-actor validation. Normative RFC coverage (4 sub-requirements): RFC 6750, RFC 7662, RFC 8705, RFC 9068, RFC 9449.

RFC gaps (1 of 8): Security consequences of artifact compromise. Partial RFC coverage (4): Transfer and forwarding assumptions; Storage and disclosure assumptions; Derivation and re-delegation assumptions; Audience and context restrictions. Normative RFC coverage (3 sub-requirements): RFC 6750, RFC 7800, RFC 8705, RFC 9449, RFC 9700.
RFC gaps (2 of 7): Runtime or workload-context binding; Rotation and failure behavior for binding credentials. Normative RFC coverage (5 sub-requirements): RFC 7800, RFC 8705, RFC 9449.

RFC gaps (3 of 6): Formal attenuation algebra; Monotonic attenuation guarantee; Verifiable proof that downstream authority is bounded by upstream authority. Partial RFC coverage (3): Scope narrowing during token exchange; Structured authorization narrowing via authorization_details; Authority aggregation / co-delegation.

RFC gaps (4 of 6): Explicit permission to re-delegate; Explicit prohibition of re-delegation; Delegation depth limits; Downstream authority inheritance rules for re-delegated tokens. Partial RFC coverage (2): Token transformation enabling authority propagation; Actor chain representation for multi-hop exchange.

RFC gaps (5 of 7): Execution provenance; Invocation provenance; Tool invocation provenance; Human approval provenance; Provenance disclosure semantics. Partial RFC coverage (2): Delegation provenance; Runtime retrieval of provenance metadata.

RFC gaps (8 of 9): Human approval checkpoints during delegated execution; Semantics of approval denial, interruption, or override during execution; Human oversight policies; Classification of delegated actions as autonomous vs. supervised; Binding of a human approval to the exact delegated action and its parameters; Approval validity window and invalidation when the action, parameters or context change between approval and execution; Approver unavailability; Control of approval request volume, grouping and presentation. Normative RFC coverage (1 sub-requirements): RFC 6749, RFC 9635.

RFC gaps (3 of 8): Delegation ancestry validation failure semantics; Unauthorized re-delegation or delegation-depth violations; Human approval failure semantics. Partial RFC coverage (2): Authorization-details failure handling; Binding or proof-of-possession validation failures. Normative RFC coverage (3 sub-requirements): RFC 6750, RFC 7662, RFC 8693.
